cards.front: What is the function of the cell membrane?
cards.back: Controls movement of substances in/out of the cell. Partially permeable.

cards.front: Name the organelle responsible for protein synthesis.
cards.back: Ribosomes. Can be free in cytoplasm or attached to rough ER.

cards.front: What is the function of mitochondria?
cards.back: Site of aerobic respiration. Produces ATP for cellular energy.

cards.front: Which organelle contains the genetic material in eukaryotic cells?
cards.back: Nucleus. Contains chromosomes (DNA) and controls cell activities.

cards.front: What is the function of the cell wall in plant cells?
cards.back: Provides structural support and protection. Made of cellulose. Fully permeable.

cards.front: Where does photosynthesis occur in plant cells?
cards.back: Chloroplasts. Contain chlorophyll which absorbs light energy.

cards.front: What is the function of the vacuole in plant cells?
cards.back: Maintains turgor pressure, stores nutrients/waste, helps cell growth. Contains cell sap.

cards.front: Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells: which has a nucleus?
cards.back: Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus. Prokaryotic cells have DNA free in cytoplasm (nucleoid region).

cards.front: A student observes a cell under a microscope. It has a cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole. What type of cell is it?
cards.back: Plant cell. Animal cells lack cell walls, chloroplasts, and have only small vacuoles.

cards.front: Calculate the magnification: Image size = 15mm, Actual size = 0.03mm
What is the role of the cytoplasm?
cards.back: Jelly-like substance where most chemical reactions occur. Contains enzymes for metabolic reactions.

cards.front: Which organelle modifies and packages proteins for secretion?
cards.back: Golgi apparatus (Golgi body). Receives proteins from rough ER, modifies them, packages into vesicles.

cards.front: What is the function of lysosomes?
cards.back: Contain digestive enzymes. Break down waste materials, worn-out organelles, and ingested pathogens.

cards.front: Explain the difference between rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
cards.back: Rough ER has ribosomes on surface - site of protein synthesis. Smooth ER lacks ribosomes - site of lipid/steroid synthesis and detoxification.

cards.front: Why do muscle cells have many mitochondria?
cards.back: Muscle contraction requires large amounts of ATP. More mitochondria = more aerobic respiration = more ATP production.
